# Implementation Plan: Web Calculator

## Overview

This plan builds the web calculator in two ordered halves connected by the typed REST contract. Per SEED.md, the backend math engine is implemented and verified first (Python 3.11+ / FastAPI with exact `decimal.Decimal` arithmetic), then the frontend (React + TypeScript / Vite). Each task builds incrementally on prior tasks, ending with wiring that leaves no orphaned code. Property-based tests (Hypothesis on the backend, table/generator-driven on the frontend) validate the correctness properties defined in the design, and example-based tests cover documented behaviors and edge cases.

- Tasks marked with `*` are optional test sub-tasks and can be skipped for a faster MVP; core implementation tasks are never optional.
- Each task references specific requirement clauses for traceability, and each property test task references its property number from the design.
- Checkpoints ensure incremental validation; the backend is fully implemented and verified before frontend work begins (per SEED.md).
- Property-based tests use Hypothesis (backend, ≥100 iterations, tagged) and generator/table-driven cases (frontend reducer); example-based tests cover documented behaviors and edge cases.
- Full WCAG conformance requires manual testing with assistive technologies and expert review, which the automated checks supplement but do not replace.

## Stage 2 Tasks (Scientific Calculator Extension)

Stage 2 extends the same web-calculator spec into a scientific calculator. All Stage 1 tasks above remain in force and unchanged. Per the SEED-2 "Instructions for AI Agents", work proceeds backend-first: Step 1 Stage 1 inspection remediation (Requirement 16), Step 2 the backend Evaluation_Engine extension (tokenizer/parser/evaluator/scientific/constants/errors) and API, Step 3 the frontend local state (angle mode, memory register, calculation history) and hooks, Step 4 the UI surfaces (scientific keypad, history panel, memory indicator, angle toggle) with responsive, accessible styling. Each task builds on prior tasks and ends wired into `Calculator.tsx`, leaving no orphaned code. New tokens, grammar productions, AST nodes, and evaluator operations are purely additive and must not weaken Requirements 1–15 (Requirement 16.3).

- [ ] 16. Remediate Stage 1 inspection findings and lock them with tests
  - Apply the optional cosmetic remediations recorded in the design's "Stage 1 Codebase Inspection Report": correct the Stage 1 design precedence prose to `+ -` < `* /` < unary `-` < `^` < parentheses (documentation-only, no code change), and optionally improve the malformed-number message in `tokenizer.py`/`parser.py` (e.g. detect adjacent NUMBER tokens or a lexeme with two dots and raise `InvalidSyntaxError` "Malformed number near position N") WITHOUT changing which inputs are accepted or rejected (preserve Requirement 4.2 behavior)
  - Preserve every Stage 1 acceptance criterion (Requirements 1–15); if any remediation regresses a Stage 1 criterion, revert or correct it before continuing
  - [ ]* 16.1 Write regression-safe pytest for the remediated engine-affecting behavior
    - Add `backend/tests/test_inspection_fixes.py` asserting the corrected malformed-number behavior still returns a 4xx Error_Response with no result (Requirement 4.2 unchanged) and that the full Stage 1 suite continues to pass with zero failures/errors
    - _Requirements: 16.1, 16.2, 16.3, 16.4, 16.5, 16.6_

import "./CalcButton.css";

/**
 * Semantic grouping for a calculator control, used to hook variant-specific
 * styling (e.g., color-coding operators vs. digits). Styling itself is the
 * responsibility of the theme task; this component only exposes the class hook.
 */
export type CalcButtonVariant = "digit" | "operator" | "action";

/**
 * Props for {@link CalcButton}.
 *
 * The component renders a native `<button>`, so keyboard operability and the
 * implicit `role="button"` are inherent (Requirement 12.2 — no explicit role is
 * needed on a native button). Focus is never suppressed.
 */
export interface CalcButtonProps {
  /**
   * Visible text identifying the button's function, e.g. `"7"`, `"+"`, `"="`.
   * Rendered inside the button so every control carries a visible label
   * (Requirement 11.6).
   */
  label: string;
  /**
   * Accessible label describing the button's function in words (e.g. `"plus"`,
   * `"divide"`, `"equals"`, `"clear"`) rather than only the symbol. It must
   * correspond to the visible function (Requirement 12.1). When omitted, it
   * falls back to {@link CalcButtonProps.label} so the accessible name always
   * matches the visible label.
   */
  ariaLabel?: string;
  /** Invoked when the button is activated by click, touch, or keyboard. */
  onActivate: () => void;
  /** Optional additional class names appended to the button's class list. */
  className?: string;
  /** Semantic grouping used as a styling hook. Defaults to `"digit"`. */
  variant?: CalcButtonVariant;
}

/**
 * A single calculator key rendered as a native `<button>`.
 *
 * - Shows a visible label identifying its function (Requirement 11.6).
 * - Exposes an `aria-label` matching that function, describing it in words
 *   (Requirement 12.1); as a native button its `role="button"` is implicit
 *   (Requirement 12.2).
 * - Indicates its pressed/active state visually. The active-state indication is
 *   driven by CSS `:active` / `:focus-visible` hooks in `CalcButton.css`
 *   (Requirement 11.5); focus is left intact for keyboard operation.
 */
export function CalcButton({
  label,
  ariaLabel,
  onActivate,
  className,
  variant = "digit",
}: CalcButtonProps) {
  const classes = ["calc-button", `calc-button--${variant}`];
  if (className) {
    classes.push(className);
  }

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={classes.join(" ")}
      aria-label={ariaLabel ?? label}
      onClick={onActivate}
    >
      {label}
    </button>
  );
}

export default CalcButton;

/*
 * Structural CSS Grid arrangement for the physical-calculator keypad
 * (Requirements 8.1-8.3). This file owns only the grid *structure*: the named
 * areas that place digits 1-9 in a 3x3 block (7-8-9 / 4-5-6 / 1-2-3), the `0`
 * in the row below that block, and the operators in a dedicated column region
 * separated from the digit keypad. Full contrast/responsive theming (sizing,
 * color, touch targets) is delivered by the styling task (Task 13).
 */

.keypad {
  display: grid;
  /*
   * Four columns: three for the digit keypad plus one dedicated operator
   * column on the right (Requirement 8.3).
   *
   * Rows:
   *   1: parentheses spanning the digit columns + divide
   *   2: 7 8 9 + multiply
   *   3: 4 5 6 + minus
   *   4: 1 2 3 + plus
   *   5: 0 (spans two digit columns) . + clear
   *   6: equals
   */
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:
    "klparen krparen krparen kdiv"
    "k7      k8      k9      kmul"
    "k4      k5      k6      ksub"
    "k1      k2      k3      kadd"
    "k0      k0      kdot    kclear"
    "kequals kequals kequals kequals";
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

/* Digit 3x3 block: 7-8-9 / 4-5-6 / 1-2-3 (Requirement 8.2). */
.keypad__key--k7 { grid-area: k7; }
.keypad__key--k8 { grid-area: k8; }
.keypad__key--k9 { grid-area: k9; }
.keypad__key--k4 { grid-area: k4; }
.keypad__key--k5 { grid-area: k5; }
.keypad__key--k6 { grid-area: k6; }
.keypad__key--k1 { grid-area: k1; }
.keypad__key--k2 { grid-area: k2; }
.keypad__key--k3 { grid-area: k3; }

/* `0` positioned in the row below the 1-9 keypad (Requirement 8.2). */
.keypad__key--k0 { grid-area: k0; }
.keypad__key--kdot { grid-area: kdot; }

/* Parentheses (Requirement 8.1). */
.keypad__key--klparen { grid-area: klparen; }
.keypad__key--krparen { grid-area: krparen; }

/* Operators in a dedicated column region separated from the digits (Requirement 8.3). */
.keypad__key--kdiv { grid-area: kdiv; }
.keypad__key--kmul { grid-area: kmul; }
.keypad__key--ksub { grid-area: ksub; }
.keypad__key--kadd { grid-area: kadd; }

/* Evaluate and reset controls (Requirement 8.1). */
.keypad__key--kclear { grid-area: kclear; }
.keypad__key--kequals { grid-area: kequals; }

/* ==========================================================================
 * Responsive theming for the keypad grid (Task 13; Requirements 9.1-9.4, 8.4).
 * The named grid areas above define the *structure*; the rules below set the
 * fluid gap and equal-height rows so the whole keypad fits without horizontal
 * overflow or clipping at every breakpoint, and every key stays >= 44x44px on
 * mobile (enforced per-button in CalcButton.css).
 * ========================================================================== */

.keypad {
  /* Token-driven fluid gap (clamp) so keys stay separated without overflow. */
  gap: var(--gap);
  /* Equal-height rows sized to at least the touch-target floor; they grow to
     fill available height so the keypad is comfortable on larger viewports
     while never shrinking a key below 44px (Req 9.4). Uses grid-auto-rows so
     every templated row (parentheses, digits, operators, 0/., equals) matches. */
  grid-auto-rows: minmax(var(--touch-min), 1fr);
  width: 100%;
}

/* Mobile (320-767px): keep the four-column layout but tighten the gap so three
   digit columns + one operator column fit at 320px with no horizontal overflow
   and no clipped keys (Req 9.1, 9.4). */
@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .keypad {
    gap: clamp(0.3rem, 1.5vw, 0.5rem);
  }
}

/* Tablet / desktop (>=768px): a touch more breathing room between keys while
   the panel width cap in global.css prevents overflow (Req 9.2, 9.3). */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .keypad {
    gap: 0.6rem;
  }
}

import type { AngleMode } from "../api/types";
import CalcButton from "./CalcButton";

/**
 * Props for {@link AngleModeToggle}.
 *
 * Presentational component: the Calculator container (task 35.3) owns the
 * `angleMode` state and the flip logic. This control only DISPLAYS the active
 * mode (Requirement 22.6) and calls `onToggle` on activation to request a flip
 * (Requirement 22.7).
 */
export interface AngleModeToggleProps {
  /** The currently active angle unit for trigonometric evaluation. */
  angleMode: AngleMode;
  /**
   * Requests a flip to the other angle mode. The container flips the mode in
   * React state; that update is synchronous on click and re-renders immediately,
   * well within the 100 ms update budget (Requirement 22.7), so simply invoking
   * this callback satisfies the timing requirement.
   */
  onToggle: () => void;
}

/**
 * A toggle control that displays the active angle mode and flips it on
 * activation.
 *
 * - Displays the active mode as a short visible label — `RAD` for radians,
 *   `DEG` for degrees (Requirement 22.6).
 * - On activation it calls {@link AngleModeToggleProps.onToggle}; the container
 *   updates state immediately, so the displayed mode updates within 100 ms
 *   (Requirement 22.7).
 * - Reuses the Stage 1 {@link CalcButton} accessibility pattern (native
 *   `<button>`, visible label + matching `aria-label`, inherited focus/pressed
 *   state). The accessible name communicates both the current mode and that
 *   activating switches it (e.g. "Angle mode: radians. Activate to switch to
 *   degrees."). Uses the `action` variant.
 */
export function AngleModeToggle({ angleMode, onToggle }: AngleModeToggleProps) {
  const isRadians = angleMode === "radians";
  const label = isRadians ? "RAD" : "DEG";
  const otherMode = isRadians ? "degrees" : "radians";
  const ariaLabel = `Angle mode: ${angleMode}. Activate to switch to ${otherMode}.`;

  return (
    <CalcButton
      label={label}
      ariaLabel={ariaLabel}
      onActivate={onToggle}
      variant="action"
      className="angle-mode-toggle"
    />
  );
}

export default AngleModeToggle;

/**
 * Typed API contract for the Evaluate_Endpoint (`POST /api/v1/evaluate`).
 *
 * These types mirror the backend's Pydantic schemas and the JSON contract
 * documented in the design's API Contract section. The response is modeled as
 * a discriminated union whose two members are distinguished purely by the
 * presence of a string `result` field (success) or a string `error` field
 * (error) — success and error payloads are mutually exclusive.
 *
 * Requirements: 13.1, 13.2, 13.3, 13.4, 13.5
 */

/**
 * Selectable angle unit for trigonometric evaluation. Modeled as a restricted
 * literal union that mirrors the backend's `Literal["radians", "degrees"]`, so
 * only these two values are representable in the typed contract (Requirement
 * 24.6).
 */
export type AngleMode = "radians" | "degrees";

/**
 * Request payload sent to the Evaluate_Endpoint (Requirements 13.1, 24.6). The
 * `angleMode` field selects the angle unit for trigonometric evaluation. The
 * API client serializes it to the backend's snake_case `angle_mode` field; the
 * serialization itself lives in `client.ts` — this is purely the typed contract.
 */
export interface EvaluateRequest {
  expression: string;
  angleMode: AngleMode;
}

/** Successful evaluation response (Requirement 13.2). */
export interface EvaluateSuccess {
  result: string;
}

/** Structured error response (Requirement 13.3). */
export interface ErrorResponse {
  error: string;
}

/**
 * The full set of shapes the endpoint is contracted to return. A conforming
 * response is exactly one of these two members (Requirement 5.5).
 */
export type EvaluateResponse = EvaluateSuccess | ErrorResponse;

/**
 * The Memory_Register value. Held as a decimal string rather than a JavaScript
 * number so the backend's exact-decimal precision is preserved verbatim with no
 * float coercion (Requirement 24.6).
 */
export interface MemoryState {
  value: string;
}

/**
 * A single Calculation_History entry pairing a submitted expression with the
 * backend result string (Requirement 24.6).
 */
export interface HistoryEntry {
  expression: string;
  result: string;
}

/**
 * The session Calculation_History: a read-only list of {@link HistoryEntry}
 * records ordered newest-first and capped at 100 entries. The ordering and the
 * cap are enforced by the history reducer (task 32); this type only expresses
 * the immutable shape (Requirement 24.6).
 */
export type CalculationHistory = readonly HistoryEntry[];

/**
 * Narrows an arbitrary value to a record so individual fields can be inspected
 * without resorting to the `any` type (Requirement 13.4).
 */
function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null;
}

/**
 * Runtime type guard for {@link EvaluateSuccess}. Validates that the value is
 * an object carrying a string `result` field (Requirement 13.5). A value that
 * also carries an `error` field is not treated as a success, keeping the
 * success/error distinction unambiguous (Requirement 5.5).
 */
export function isSuccess(r: unknown): r is EvaluateSuccess {
  return isRecord(r) && typeof r.result === "string" && !("error" in r);
}

/**
 * Runtime type guard for {@link ErrorResponse}. Validates that the value is an
 * object carrying a string `error` field (Requirement 13.5). A value that also
 * carries a `result` field is not treated as an error, keeping the
 * success/error distinction unambiguous (Requirement 5.5).
 */
export function isError(r: unknown): r is ErrorResponse {
  return isRecord(r) && typeof r.error === "string" && !("result" in r);
}

/**
 * Pure state management for the session Calculation_History.
 *
 * This reducer owns ONLY the ordered list of completed calculations surfaced in
 * the History_Panel. It stores {@link HistoryEntry} records newest-first and
 * exposes them for rendering; it performs no arithmetic and no network I/O.
 *
 * Append-on-success only (Requirement 21.7): the reducer appends an entry solely
 * when it receives a `HISTORY_APPEND` action, and the container/`useEvaluator`
 * (tasks 33 / 35.3) is responsible for dispatching that action ONLY on a
 * successful backend result — it is never dispatched on an error response, so an
 * error leaves the history unchanged. The reducer itself stays pure and simply
 * prepends whatever entry it is handed.
 *
 * Selecting a history entry's expression or result to replace the entire current
 * expression (Requirements 21.3, 21.4) is wired in the container via the
 * `calculatorReducer`; this reducer only stores and exposes entries and MUST NOT
 * mutate any expression state.
 *
 * Requirements: 21.1, 21.2, 21.3, 21.4, 21.5, 21.6, 21.7, 21.8
 */

import type { CalculationHistory, HistoryEntry } from '../api/types';

/**
 * Maximum number of entries the Calculation_History retains. When an append
 * would exceed this cap, the oldest entry (the last element, since the list is
 * newest-first) is dropped so the list never holds more than this many entries
 * (Requirements 21.1, 21.5).
 */
export const MAX_HISTORY = 100;

/**
 * The complete history state: a read-only, newest-first list of calculation
 * entries. Using {@link CalculationHistory} directly (rather than wrapping it in
 * an object) keeps the state minimal and immutable.
 *
 * Empty (`[]`) in the initial state before any successful evaluation, which the
 * History_Panel renders as an empty-state indication (Requirement 21.8).
 */
export type HistoryState = CalculationHistory;

/**
 * The initial, empty history (Requirement 21.8). No entries are present until a
 * successful evaluation is appended by the container.
 */
export const initialHistory: CalculationHistory = [];

/**
 * The set of actions the Calculation_History can dispatch.
 *
 * String literal `type` discriminants form a discriminated union so the reducer
 * can exhaustively narrow each case with no use of `any`.
 */
export type HistoryAction =
  /**
   * Prepend a completed calculation to the front of the list (newest-first,
   * Requirement 21.2), capping the list at {@link MAX_HISTORY} by dropping the
   * oldest entry (Requirements 21.1, 21.5). Dispatched by the container only on a
   * successful backend result, never on an error (Requirement 21.7).
   */
  | { type: 'HISTORY_APPEND'; entry: HistoryEntry }
  /** Clear the entire history, returning it to the empty state (Requirement 21.6). */
  | { type: 'HISTORY_CLEAR' };

/**
 * Compile-time exhaustiveness guard. If a new {@link HistoryAction} variant is
 * added without a matching `case`, the `never`-typed parameter fails to
 * type-check, flagging the missing branch. At runtime an unhandled action leaves
 * state unchanged.
 */
function assertNever(
  _action: never,
  state: CalculationHistory,
): CalculationHistory {
  return state;
}

/**
 * Pure reducer computing the next {@link HistoryState} from the current state and
 * an action. It performs no side effects and never mutates the input list —
 * every transition returns a new read-only array.
 */
export function historyReducer(
  state: CalculationHistory,
  action: HistoryAction,
): CalculationHistory {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'HISTORY_APPEND': {
      // Prepend the new entry so the list stays newest-first (Requirement 21.2),
